children: The euro falls further after the European Central Bank raised the key rate by a quarter point to 2.50%, as widely expected. The decision "had been clearly signaled by policymakers ahead of time and was fully discounted by financial markets," Capital Economics'Andrew Kenningham says in a note. The euro falls 0.3% on the day to $1.1594 following the decision, from $1.1617 beforehand, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
